business_scope.primary_industry_name: Dry Bulk Marine Transport and Brokerage of Granular Elemental Sulfur

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Federal_State; Quebec civil law for private law matters, federal common law framework for public and regulatory matters)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA) signed 2012, not yet in force
Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) with the European Union
Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA) in force July 1, 2020 (no separate BIT with US)
Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (TCA) in force April 1, 2021
Canada-Israel Free Trade Agreement (CIFTA) modernized protocol in force September 1, 2020 (context of international commodity trade)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Criminal Code of Canada (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-46), Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended), Income Tax Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.)) Part XVIII.1 mandatory disclosure rules, Quebec Business Corporations Act (CQLR c S-31.1) sections 22-23 and 158-160, Quebec Act respecting the Registraire des entreprises (CQLR c R-3.1.2), An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), Canada Business Corporations Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-44) section 21 and regulations, and FINTRAC Guidance on politically exposed persons and ownership information

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Corporate Status or Certificate of Incumbency (foreign entity evidence, if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Government registration authority in the jurisdiction of incorporation of any non-Quebec shareholder entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the Convention de La Haye of 5 October 1961, accepted by Canada as of January 1, 2024; Consular Legalization only for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized statutory declaration of beneficial ownership (UBO declaration, including intermediate entities)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or lawyer authorized to attest in Quebec under the Act respecting the Barreau du Québec and the Notaries Act (CQLR c N-3)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if executed outside Canada; notarial attestation registration in the Quebec register of personal and movable real rights only if security interests are created (not for standalone UBO declarations)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copies of passports or national identity documents of directors, officers, and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national passport/identity authority in the country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; Consular legalization for non-Hague states; translation by a certified translator under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) section 35 for documents submitted in English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Letter of reference or no-activity declaration issued by the foreign corporate registry for each non-Canadian corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry or corporate registrar of the foreign jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions), with translation and legalization in Quebec if used for Relevé d'entreprise

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all named directors, officers, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against the consolidated Canadian sanctions list under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act (Global Affairs Canada), the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) sanctions list, the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) screening requirements including heads of state, heads of government, ministers, deputy ministers, ambassadors, high-ranking military officers, and directors of state-owned enterprises; mandatory OFAC SDN screening for USD-denominated transactions and counterparty US nexus; mandatory UN Security Council sanctions screening; and mandatory review against the Corruption of Foreign Public Officials Act (S.C. 1998, c. 34) to identify heightened risk of bribery and money laundering in procurement and mineral trading contexts.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises (Entreprises Québec / Relevé d'entreprise) online portal, accessible via https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca, in conjunction with the federal Canadian Business Corporations Act online filing centre (services.ic.gc.ca) if a federal name is sought; the provincial NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) search must be completed through an accredited NUANS provider in Quebec.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), every Quebec company name must be in French, either solely in French or in a bilingual form with French having equal or greater prominence; an English designation (Inc., Corp., Ltée) is permitted alongside the French designation 'Ltée' or 'Inc.' but the French form must appear first in the corporate name; transliteration of a foreign or Latin-script name must respect strict French phonetics and avoid any token that is contrary to the French language; a company with a name in a non-Latin script must transliterate into French for registration purposes; limited exceptions apply for recognized trademark names registered under the Trademarks Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. T-13).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Souverain' or 'Royal' (requiring letter from the Crown or applying entity, prior approval by the Lieutenant-Governor in Council)
'Banque', 'Bank', 'Bancaire' (prior approval of the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions Canada under the Bank Act)
'Assurance' or 'Insurance' (prior approval of the Autorité des marchés financiers under the Insurance Companies Act and the Quebec Act respecting insurance)
'Bourse' or 'Stock Exchange' (prior approval of the Autorité des marchés financiers)
'Canada' or 'Canadien' or any suggestion of federal government sponsorship (requires special justification and approval by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
'Québec' or 'Quebec' (when used to suggest government affiliation; prior ministerial authorization required)
'Université' or 'University' (prior approval from the Minister of Higher Education)
'Commission' or 'Council' (when likely to mislead as to governmental or regulatory origin)
'coopératif' or 'cooperative' (restricted under the Cooperatives Act, CQLR c C-67.2)
'Fiducie' or 'Trust' (restricted under trust and fiduciary licensing regimes)

'pétrole' or 'oil', 'gaz' or 'gas', 'mining' or 'mini' (sensitive resource-sector tokens requiring proof of lawful licensed activity; for sulfur mineral ore trading, prior attestations of statutory compliance under the Mining Act, CQLR c M-13.1 are prudent, although the trading activity itself is not licensed)

'viticole' or 'vin' and designated premium marks, 'santé' or 'health', 'pharmaceutique' or 'pharmaceutical', 'avocat' or 'lawyer', 'notaire' or 'notary', 'comptable' or 'accountant' (regulated professional tokens requiring membership in the relevant professional order)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registraire des entreprises rejects the proposed name, the applicant may, within 30 days of refusal, file a written request for review under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1) sections 49-52, addressed to the Director of the Registraire des entreprises, including the Relevé d'entreprise rejection notice, NUANS search report, a legal opinion on distinctiveness and French-language compliance, and any trademark evidence; if the Director maintains the refusal, the applicant may apply for judicial review in the Superior Court of Quebec within the 60-day limitation period provided for by the Code of Civil Procedure (CQLR c C-25.01) articles 525-530, and may request an injunction and a name rectification order; for federal incorporations, the same appeal is administratively routed to the Director General of Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada, under subsection 12(4) of the Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001 (SOR/2001-512), with a final appeal to the Federal Court under section 18.1 of the Federal Courts Act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under section 22(1) of the Quebec Business Corporations Act (CQLR c S-31.1), a registered office address must be a physical location in Quebec capable of receiving service of process and official notices; a virtual office is not permitted as a substitute for the registered office, but a commercial virtual receptionist service may operate alongside the registered office provided the registered address is a live street address in Quebec; the company must also maintain a 'place of business' or use a registered agent in Quebec; for a mineral ore trading intermediary, a stand-alone virtual office is generally deemed insufficient to establish commercial substance and may trigger anti-avoidance scrutiny by Revenu Québec for GST/HST registration and for the cross-border income tax treaty entitlement claims.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low_to_Medium_Risk_Quantified_15_percent: Revenu Québec and the Registraire des entreprises conduct unannounced on-site inspections primarily for active trade-sector enterprises; for a Quebec-registered mineral trading company with modest physical presence and high gross revenue flows, the probability of a physical inspection within the first 18 months is approximately 15 percent, and increases if the company files for input tax credits involving federal GST/HST or if it engages in inter-provincial dry bulk marine logistics; the registry maintains no obligation to notify prior to inspection and inspectors may verify the existence of the registered office, corporate records, and accounting books.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registraire des entreprises via accredited NUANS provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Regulation respecting the fees payable to the Registraire des entreprises (CQLR c E-12.2, r. ...); prevailing market rate CAD 45-65 (USD equivalent)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Quebec provincial incorporation filing fee under the Quebec Business Corporations Act (articles of incorporation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff set by Order-in-Council under s. 159 of the Quebec Business Corporations Act and the Regulation respecting fees (approx. CAD 300-400); current indicative fee CAD 400-500 (USD 340)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee under the Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001, section 26(1) fee table: CAD 200 for online incorporation (USD 200)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate minute book and registered office records preparation (statutory record-keeping bundle, physical register in Quebec)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Incorporation service provider retained by the law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark CAD 100-250 (USD 75-190); minimum professional documentation bundle cost basis

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial ownership due diligence and UBO piercing analysis (FINTRAC-compliant CDD/KYC file including ownership chain, PEP/sanctions screening, and 25% threshold verification)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance due diligence provider or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark hourly rate CAD 200-400 per hour; flat fee for standard low-risk trading entity, 2-4 hours

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed AML screening data provider (e.g., Thomson Reuters / Dow Jones / LexisNexis) and the law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing per-record benchmark USD 20-60 per individual; compliance bundle of 5 named persons at discounted rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille bundle for foreign passport / corporate status / UBO statutory declaration (per non-Canadian beneficial owner bundle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and competent authority for apostille in the foreign jurisdiction; certified translator in Quebec additionally
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Article 30-35 Notarial tariff of the Quebec Notaries Act (CQLR c N-3) plus foreign notarial/consular fee benchmark; local market rates USD 50-150 notary, USD 150-250 apostille/consular legalization, translation CAD 60-150

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: French-language corporate governance translation / certificate of compliance with the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator of the Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interprètes agréés du Québec (OTTIAQ)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Member tariff in Quebec, standard rate CAD 45-75 per 150 words plus certificate of translation at CAD 20-40 (USD 95)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office physical address and service-of-process agent for first year (Quebec commercial leased registered address)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark CAD 300-500 per year (USD 210-350); annual fee for location with mail forwarding and statutory service acceptance

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (Loi sur les sociétés par actions), CQLR c S-31.1, especially ss. 34-35, 49, 166; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss. 4-7, 102 (if federal incorporation with extra-provincial registration in Quebec)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (statuts constitutifs) filed in the Registre des entreprises; Certificate of Constitution (certificat de constitution) issued upon filing
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the QBCA; share capital is as set out in the articles. No escrow account is required for cash subscriptions; for non-cash consideration, a contribution report (rapport de contribution) must be filed with the Registrar concurrently with or within 30 days of issuance of shares, and any later-payment obligations must be noted on the share register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT: (1) The share subscription and any contribution report for the shares of the Corporation are approved; the directors are authorized to allot and issue the subscribed shares and to record the share register accordingly. (2) The registered office is established at the address stated in the initial filing, and the Registraire des entreprises du Québec is instructed to file the notice of office. (3) The persons named in the subscription/nomination are appointed as Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, each to serve until the next annual meeting. (4) The President and Secretary are authorized to effect all filings and banking arrangements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Online Name Declaration Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a legal name search through the Registraire des entreprises' central registry and the Canadian Trademarks Database. File a name declaration (déclaration de dénomination sociale) online or submit a name reservation request. Ensure the proposed corporate name is in French or bilingual, is distinct, and does not contain prohibited expressions such as 'Bank', 'Royal', or 'Quebec'.
required_dossiers: Name search report from the Registre central des entreprises
Proof of payment of the name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, correct the objectionable element, file a revised name declaration, or request an administrative review by the Registraire des entreprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholder(s) with professional legal or notarial assistance as required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the French-language (or bilingual) Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate name, the head office address in Quebec, the maximum number and classes of shares with their rights and restrictions, any restrictions on share transfers, the number of directors, and any limitations on the corporation's activities. The articles must be executed by the subscribing founders in accordance with QBCA ss. 34-35.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation (French or bilingual)
Nomination of first directors and initial registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the draft is defective, amend the articles to match Registraire requirements and re-execute; request clarifications from the legal profiler or the Registraire's technical assistance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – secure online filing portal 'Dépôt en ligne'
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Articles of Incorporation electronically via the Registraire's online transmission system. Pay the statutory constitution fee by credit card or electronic funds transfer. Retain the electronic acknowledgement and the assigned enterprise number (NEQ). The system will validate the file and forward it for processing.
required_dossiers: Payment confirmation of the statutory filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected, review the deficiencies notice, correct the identified errors, and resubmit within 30 days; or request a formal reconsideration by the Registraire's head office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Constitution and Commencement of Existence
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, retrieve the Certificate of Constitution (certificat de constitution) and the official registry entry from the Registraire's online system. The corporation comes into existence on the date stated on the certificate. Verify the NEQ, corporate name, registered office, and director information on the certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Constitution in PDF format
Confirmation of the Registre des entreprises registration page
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains errors, file a request for correction with the Registraire under QBCA s. 37; if issuance is delayed, escalate to the Registraire's customer service with the filing acknowledgement number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Organizational Meeting, Adoption of By-laws and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first directors' meeting, adopt the by-laws, approve the share allotment and issuance, appoint officers (e.g. CEO, CFO, Secretary), confirm the registered office, and authorize banking arrangements and tax filings. Record all resolutions in the corporate minute book and have the minutes signed by the chairperson and secretary.
required_dossiers: Share subscription agreements and contribution report
Consents of directors and officers to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director dissents, record the dissent; if a quorum is lacking, postpone the meeting and obtain a written waiver of notice or consent resolution from all directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registrations with CRA and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for a Business Number (BN) with the CRA using Business Registration Online; register for corporate income tax, GST/HST (when taxable supplies exceed C$30,000), and an import/export account (RM/PD) for cross-border trade. Register for Quebec QST and any required ministerial permits through the Entreprises Québec portal or Revenu Québec online services. File the initial declaration of registration with the Registraire des entreprises and arrange annual enterprise registration renewals.
required_dossiers: Completed CRA/Revenu Québec tax registration forms
Proof of registered office address in Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tax account is denied or queried, contact CRA or Revenu Québec, provide corrections, and re-file; a corporate resolution appointing an authorized agent may be required to resolve identity verification issues.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No specific industrial licensing board applies to dry bulk trading and brokerage of elemental sulfur; if physical warehousing or transshipment is contemplated, the Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) is the relevant permitting authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating license required for trading and brokerage; an import/export permit under the Export and Import Permits Act (Canada) may be required for cross-border movement of sulfur.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for pure trading and brokerage; if causing storage or handling of sulfur, the activity may require a declaration of conformity (registration) or a full impact assessment under the Environmental Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2) depending on actual footprint and risk.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For any incidental storage or transfer, comply with CQLR c Q-2 and municipal stormwater permits: stormwater contact must be contained, pH maintained 6.0-9.5, total suspended solids ≤30 mg/L, no free-flowing sulfur particles; atmospheric SO2 concentration not to exceed 150 ppm and fugitive particulate matter below 10 mg/m³ at the property boundary; waste sulfur must be handled as a residual material under the Regulation respecting residual materials.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (certificat de sécurité incendie) from the local fire safety service; structural load inspection under the National Building Code – Canada (Quebec Part 3) if any sulfur storage occurs; workplace clearance from the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) confirming compliance with the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c S-2.1) for dust, ventilation, and personal protective equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for GST/HST and federal tax; Revenu Québec for QST and provincial tax. Portals: CRA 'My Business Account' and Revenu Québec 'Mon dossier d'entreprise'.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must first obtain a federal/Quebec enterprise registration, then apply to the CRA for a Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account using Form RC1 or online through the Business Registration Online service. For Quebec, the entity must register with Revenu Québec for QST and provincial obligations using Form LM-101-V (GST/HST and QST complex registration), providing Quebec Business Identifier (NEQ). Non-resident corporations may also require an income tax TIN through Form RC214 or a Canadian branch registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation with territorial application: non-resident corporations are taxable on Canadian-source business income; GST/HST applies to taxable supplies made in Canada and QST applies to taxable supplies made in Quebec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: For GST/HST: GST/HST registration group election (Excise Tax Act s.156), closely related corporation election (s.150), and joint election for supplies of exempt property. For income tax: non-resident corporation can elect under subsection 216(1) for rental income; no US-style check-the-box election exists, but provincial QST grouping elections with Revenu Québec mirror the GST/HST group rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added tax) and Quebec QST (provincial value-added tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of cumulative worldwide taxable supplies (threshold under Division II of the Excise Tax Act for GST/HST and under the Quebec QST Act for QST; registration becomes mandatory once exceeded if supplying in Canada/Quebec).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No national real-time fiscal clearance or tax-authority digital stamping applies. CRA requires business records in a specified electronic or readable format (ECM standards). Quebec mandates electronic invoicing for suppliers billing Quebec public authorities and imposes specific invoicing content requirements; general B2B e-invoicing follows Revenu Québec's prescribed XML/EDI standards but without continuous transaction controls.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods that are exported from Canada, and services rendered to non-residents (or wholly performed outside Canada), quality for zero-rating under the Excise Tax Act and QST Act. The exporter must prove the goods were physically delivered to a destination outside Canada, that no resident acquired the supply before export, and maintain contemporaneous export evidence such as customs documentation, carrier transport records, sale contracts, and payment evidence. For QST, the qualifying supply must be exported from Quebec/Canada to be zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Valid commercial invoice evidencing the sale of granular sulfur
CBSA Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A or Canada Export Reporting System record)
Bill of Lading / multimodal transport document evidencing export
Carrier or freight forwarder certificate of export / destination confirmation
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank SWIFT/letter of credit payment record from the non-resident buyer
Contract specifying international commercial terms (Incoterms) and transfer of ownership
Customs export control reports (e.g., CERS transaction filing confirming customs release)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may disallow zero-rating and reassess net tax, with compound interest, if documentation is insufficient or the exporter has not demonstrated physical export. Fraudulent zero-rating claims attract penalties of 25% or more for gross negligence (Excise Tax Act s.280), 200% penalties and criminal fines/imprisonment for wilful evasion (s.281 and Income Tax Act), and extended reassessment periods up to four years or indefinitely for fraud. QST fraud penalties mirror federal exposure with interest and surcharges imposed by Revenu Québec under the Tax Administration Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a floating exchange rate regime with full convertibility for current account transactions under IMF Article VIII. Capital account transactions are generally permitted without prior approval for corporate activities. Profit remittance to foreign shareholders is unrestricted, subject only to Canadian tax withholding at source and beneficial ownership identification under the Income Tax Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds to the central bank is required under Canadian law. Exporters must receive full payment for goods. All export receipts exceeding CAD 10,000 must be reported to FINTRAC; banks may request supporting documents such as commercial invoices and bills of lading for verification.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs face significant legal constraints in Canada due to FATF compliance and anti-money laundering obligations. Cross-border fintech platforms must comply with Canadian Payment Services Regulations; remote onboarding is restricted for high-volume trade finance, favoring traditional banks for sulfur ore trade settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening and KYC via video interview is permitted for Canadian corporations under FINTRAC guidelines. However, for cross-border trade finance involving sulfur mineral ore, directors may be required to attend in-person interviews or provide notarized documents to mitigate sanctions and AML risks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening hits on beneficial owners or directors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide OFAC, UN, and EU sanctions clearance certificates, source of wealth documentation, and corporate due diligence reports

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent beneficial ownership structure disclosed in corporate filings
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit latest corporate registry extract from Quebec Enterprise Register, articles of incorporation, and shareholder agreements

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction involvement in sulfur ore supply chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide end-user certificates, trade references, and proof of legitimate commercial purpose

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections routed via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'CAP' or 'EQTY'. Verification requires source of funds letter, beneficial ownership proof, and tax clearance. Use of correspondent banks such as in the US or EU for faster processing. All transactions subject to FINTRAC reporting if exceeding thresholds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements settled through SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'TRADE' or 'SERV'. For granular elemental sulfur trade, commercial letters of credit (LCs) are standard under UCP 600. Clearing via correspondent banks in major financial centers. Purpose codes must align with actual transaction to avoid AML flags.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under sections 86-89 of the Quebec Business Corporations Act, confirming corporate name, registered office, and current directors.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days following the anniversary date of the corporation's registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing imposes an additional CAD 87.50 penalty on top of the CAD 82.50 annual fee; issuance of certificates of compliance is suspended; administrative strike-off by the Registraire occurs after two consecutive years of non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (applicable where the company is a CBCA federal corporation).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or continuance.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No graduated penalty, but default for two consecutive years permits administrative dissolution by the Director of Corporations Canada; access to compliance documents is withheld.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Corporation Income Tax Return (T2), including financial statements and tax-reconciliation schedules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal period end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month of default (maximum 12 months) under Income Tax Act s. 162(2), daily compound interest, and CRA arbitrary assessments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Corporation Income Tax Return (Form CO-17) with provincial schedules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the taxation year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Provincial late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month (maximum 12 months) under the Quebec Tax Administration Act, plus interest and ministerial reassessment powers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST return and Quebec QST return (where the corporation is an annual filer; monthly and quarterly filers remit on their normal cycle).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year end for annual filers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty of 5% of net tax plus 1% per month (maximum 12 months), minimum CAD 100, with daily interest; habitual default triggers audit and enforced collections.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit is mandatory only for a distributing corporation (public distribution of securities) under the QBCA; a closely held non-distributing sulfur-trade corporation is exempt, although shareholders holding at least 5% of issued shares may requisition an audit. Federal CBCA corporations may dispense with the auditor by unanimous shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises), which is the default for the private trading entity; tax returns (T2 / CO-17) reconcile statutory accounting income to taxable income in accordance with the Income Tax Act and the Quebec Taxation Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec does not impose a standalone annual UBO return; the REQ annual declaration is the operative annual confirmation of directors, officers, and registered address. Shareholding transfers must be recorded contemporaneously in the Register of Members and reflected in the next annual declaration. A CBCA federal corporation additionally maintains an Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register verified during the annual minute-book audit; director changes are reported to the REQ within 15 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 220 - USD 1,100 per year (CAD 300 - 1,500) for registered office and corporate secretarial agent services in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,400 - USD 22,000 per year for a full statutory audit of a private mineral-ore trading company (CAD 10,000 - 30,000); compilation and review engagements typically range USD 2,200 - 7,400

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: General combined federal and Quebec corporate income tax headline rate: 26.5%, comprising 15% federal general corporate rate after provincial abatement and 11.5% Quebec general corporate rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday, investment credit, or preferential deduction applies to a non-resident-owned federal/provincial business corporation engaged in ISIC 4669 dry-bulk mineral ore and sulfur trading. The federal small business deduction (9% federal / 3.2% Quebec) is restricted to Canadian-controlled private corporations whose proportion of taxable capital and active business income does not exceed the statutory thresholds; a wholesale trading vehicle controlled, directly or indirectly, by a non-resident will not qualify.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed through the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) digital gateway using CRA-approved EFILE software or CRA 'My Business Account'.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing due date: six months after the corporation's taxation year-end. For a December 31 year-end, the return is due by June 30 of the following calendar year. The balance-due date for federal tax remittance is two months after year-end, extended to three months for eligible qualified Canadian-controlled private corporations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CRA 15-character business identifier and federal taxation year-end date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The offshore parent must open a CRA business account; a Canadian permanent establishment is presumed when the trading entity contracts, invoices, or carries inventory in Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total sales, commissions, fees, and other trading revenue recognized under Canadian GAAP and adjusted for tax purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Canadian-source and treaty-allocable revenues; foreign-source revenues are excluded only if the corporation has no permanent establishment in Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business income or loss before special deductions, including gross profit from sulfur ore trading and brokerage commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Commissions earned for agency services rendered in Quebec are fully taxable; legal allocation among provinces may be required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 1, Line A / Cost of Goods Sold
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs of dry-bulk ore purchase, ocean freight, inland logistics, insurance, demurrage, and LC charges to the extent they reduce trading revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document all intercompany purchase prices with contemporaneous transfer pricing benchmarks; non-deductible payments to non-arm's length parties are specifically reviewed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 1, Line H / Net Business Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after all deductible operating expenses, including administrative overhead, professional fees, and regulatory compliance costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Head-office overhead charged by the foreign parent to the Canadian branch or subsidiary must satisfy the arm's length test under CRA's transfer pricing guidance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after applying non-capital loss carryforwards, capital loss restrictions, and other Part I adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations must compute taxable income only for Canadian-source income attributable to a permanent establishment and cannot deduct losses realized by a sister affiliate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross federal Part I tax before credits; the general rate is 15% after the 10% provincial abatement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned corporation, the provincial abatement is available only under Quebec treaty allocation or through a permanent establishment in Quebec.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months (maximum 17%). Repeat failure in a three-year period increases the base penalty to 10%. Gross negligence and recursive penalties may equal 50% of overstated deductions and additionally federal interest accrues at prescribed rates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Revenu Québec CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically through 'Clic Revenu' or 'Mon dossier d'entreprise' using Revenu Québec-approved software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is the same as the federal T2: six months after the fiscal year-end. For a December 31 year-end, the CO-17 must be filed by June 30. The Quebec balance-due date is two months after year-end, or three months for an eligible CCPC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 10-digit NEQ and required Quebec tax account code assigned by Revenu Québec.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation carrying on business through an establishment in Quebec must register for a Quebec enterprise number before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate gross sales and brokerage revenues in Quebec.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only trading income attributable to the Quebec permanent establishment is reportable; sales negotiated and executed outside Canada by the parent are excluded if no QC establishment exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec cost of sales, including marine freight, stevedoring, and inspection of granular sulfur cargo.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: CRA and Revenu Québec will scrutinize related-party ore purchase prices; contemporaneous functional analysis is mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income after provincial adjustments and loss-carryover claims.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Quebec allocation of taxable income is based on the gross-revenue factor and payroll factor; non-resident shareholders must compute Canadian/Quebec situs of revenue carefully.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provincial tax at the 11.5% general corporate rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty domestic rate-reduction is not available for Quebec tax unless a provincial allocation formula is met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid Quebec tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months, with a doubled 10% base for repeated non-filing. Failure to electronically file adds a separate penalty calculated per $500,000 of revenues. Negligence penalties up to 50% apply; interest compounds daily.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Canadian Income Tax Act on dividends paid by a Canadian corporation to a non-resident shareholder. This rate is determined before any applicable tax treaty reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The paying corporation must obtain a completed and signed CRA Form NR301/NR302 (or acceptable equivalent declaration) from the beneficial owner and an official Certificate of Residence / tax residence certificate issued by the competent authority of the treaty country. The Canadian payer then withholds at the reduced treaty rate (typically 5% for a corporate shareholder owning at least 10% of voting stock, 15% for portfolio dividends). If excess withholding arises, the non-resident must file a refund claim with the CRA within the statutory limitation period, ordinarily two years after the end of the calendar year of payment, and remit supporting TRC and explanation of treaty residency.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Part XIII rate for interest and royalties paid to non-residents: 25%. Under Canada's tax treaties, arm's-length interest is generally reduced to 0-15% (0% under the Canada-US and Canada-Qatar DTA where the recipient is the beneficial owner); industrial royalties (patents, trademarks, know-how) are commonly reduced to 10% or 15%, and certain literary/cultural royalties may be 0%. The reduced treaty rate is not automatic; it requires a valid TRC and, where applicable, an CRA waiver to collect less tax at source. Cross-border payments described as 'administrative fees', 'management fees', or 'consulting fees' are not exempt from Part XIII and are re-characterized as taxable Canadian-source services unless a genuine arm's-length arrangement is documented.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Form T106 (Information Return for Non-Arm's Length Transactions) must be filed with the CRA when the aggregate fair market value of reportable cross-border transactions with each non-resident related party exceeds C$1 million. CRA's T4117 transfer-pricing guidelines require a comprehensive Local File and Master File (or equivalent combined file) when controlled transactions exceed C$2 million in a taxation year; documentation should be contemporaneous and completed before the filing deadline.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not deploy a stand-alone Economic Substance Regulation statute akin to UAE ESR. However, economic substance is central to the 'real risk and control' functional analysis applied under Section 247 of the Income Tax Act and to the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under Section 245. A Quebec trading entity with no fixed business premises, no local employees involved in ocean-charter negotiation, no cargo risk, and no substantive decision-making functions will be vulnerable to treaty denial under the Principal Purpose Test (OECD MLI, Article 7) and to reassessment on the ground that the Canadian vehicle is a conduit with no commercial rationale. The CRA may reattribute the trading income to the foreign principal and assess the Canadian entity as a mere agent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting sulfur-ore trading revenue from the T2/CO-17 returns, recording fake freight or inspection invoices, issuing circular invoices between the Canadian entity and a tax-haven procurement affiliate, or knowingly failing to remit federal and Quebec corporate taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under section 239 of the Income Tax Act and section 101 of the Quebec Taxation Act: a fine of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment for up to two years. Gross negligence penalties may amount to 50% of understated income. Failure to remit source deductions under section 227.1 activates strict civil liability equal to the unremitted amount plus interest and penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are personally liable for unpaid employee source deductions and withholding tax held in trust, regardless of the corporate veil. Where the corporation is a sham or veneer used to conceal foreign beneficial ownership, courts may pierce the veil and impose joint and several civil restitution on directors. CRA criminal investigation can recommend travel-ban orders, asset-freezing seizures, and jail terms of up to two years for every month of ongoing evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing the purchase of elemental sulfur or mineral ore from a related non-resident supplier below arm's length, or paying inflated management fees, marine charter fees, or product inspection costs to a related trader in a zero-tax jurisdiction, without a contemporaneous TP study and without filing Form T106.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Section 247(3) transfer-pricing penalty equal to 10% of the net transfer-pricing adjustment where the adjustment exceeds the lesser of C$5,000,000 and 10% of gross revenue for that year. The CRA may also impose Section 161(1) arrears interest, Section 162 late-information penalties, and reassess open years. In addition, a false T106 entry carries a specific penalty under Section 162(10).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign a knowingly false T106 or TP documentation may be co-assessed under the due-diligence provisions; criminal liability attaches for forgery or fraud. The Quebec Revenue Board may allow the CRA to recover from directors where the corporation is insolvent and the director exercised effective control over pricing. Travel bans are possible where the underlying conduct is prosecuted as a criminal offence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Canadian corporation as a shell with no Canadian office, bank account, or negotiation personnel; using back-to-back contracts to pass legal title to sulfur through the Canadian entity while risk stays with the foreign principal; or claiming treaty benefits for a Quebec entity without commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR under Section 245 permits the CRA to deny the tax benefit and re-assess the entire transaction series. Misrepresentation penalties under Section 163(2) can add 50% of the understated tax. The competent authority may deny reduced treaty withholding rates under the OECD Multilateral Instrument where obtaining the treaty benefit was a principal purpose and substance is absent. Revenu Québec can similarly issue an 'artificial transaction' penalty and impose gross negligence fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for corporate tax where the corporation is used as a sham to defeat taxes; Canadian courts may impose individual liability for knowing participation in a fraudulent scheme. A Director of a non-resident parent signing Canadian filings is considered a 'resident director' for service of process, and CRA may obtain a travel-ban against the individual through the Federal Court in fraud proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML Compliance Deficit (FINTRAC / Proceeds of Crime)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Employing a secret foreign trustee or nominee director, failing to register as a money-services business (MSB) when processing LC-backed transfers, failing to report suspicious wire transactions related to open-cargo sulfur trade, or refusing to disclose the ultimate beneficial owner of the Canadian trading corporation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act: administrative monetary penalty up to C$100,000 for an individual and C$500,000 for a corporation for a first serious violation; criminal prosecution can impose imprisonment up to five years and unlimited fines. FINTRAC issues public sanctions and may name the corporation on its non-compliance list.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers can be personally fined and imprisoned for consenting to or permitting the AML violation; corporate veil protection is stripped for individuals who participate in concealing beneficial ownership. Travel bans may be ordered during an active criminal investigation if the individual is a flight risk. The 'responsible person' nominated with FINTRAC is exposed to personal civil restitution for funds laundered through the trading entity.
